title: Paranormal tours, murder mystery being offered at Van Buren County Historical Society Museum

content:
Just in time for Halloween, the Van Buren County Historical Society Museum in Hartford is offering a whole month of spooky fun with some paranormal tours of its building.

Museum President Sandy Merchant tells us the museum is housed in a brick building constructed in 1884 after a fire destroyed the county poorhouse, which originally opened in 1866. The facility housed elderly, ill, and impoverished residents until closing as a home in 1952. Merchant says it today contains 44 rooms of local history, and according to some, some supernatural inhabitants.

“We don’t think it’s inhabited by scary people,” Merchant said. “We think it’s inhabited by spirits of the people who lived here, and they’re friendly, some of them. One of the ladies does not want us in a room. But we have a gentleman who is particularly susceptible to this, seems to be the target all the time.”

That would be museum volunteer Tad Moody, who’s worked there for 20 years. Merchant says he’s had a mannequin almost fall on him and then right itself, he’s heard his name whispered, and he’s seen a fan turn itself on.

All month long, Moody is taking people on tours of the building and offering them K-2 paranormal detection meters. The tours are $10 or $25, depending on which package a visitor wants. Reservations can be made by contacting Moody at the museum.

Also, on November 1, Merchant says the museum will host a murder mystery. They’ll focus on the Morris murders from 1879.

“It was a family, husband and wife, shot and killed in Decatur. The Morrises were early settlers. They never caught the murderer. He stole the horse, took the horse to South Bend, got on a train and disappeared. And there was a serving girl in the house and said she didn’t hear a thing.”

Merchant says a whole posse looked for the killer, but the killer was never found. For the murder mystery, museum volunteers will dress up in costume as participants piece together clues.

The murder mystery will run from 2 to 4 p.m. on Sunday, November 1 and will be free. However, a donation to the museum is requested.

You can learn more about the Van Buren County Historical Society Museum at its website.
